ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, the center is labeled L, point N is on the circle; the line segment from exterior point M to point N is labeled 16, and the problem states that this line segment is tangent to the circle. The radius from center L to point of tangency N is labeled 12. The horizontal line segment from M to L is labeled x. Reasoning: Radius LN connects to point of tangency N, so LN is perpendicular to tangent MN. Therefore triangle MNL is a right triangle, with legs MN = 16 and LN = 12, and hypotenuse ML = x. By the Pythagorean theorem, x = sqrt(16^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(256 + 144) = sqrt(400) = 20.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle with center L, radius LN labeled 12, and an external tangent segment MN labeled 16 from point M touching the circle at N. The unknown x labels the straight segment ML from the external point M to the center L. Use the theorem that a radius drawn to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line, so triangle MNL is right with legs LN = 12 and MN = 16. Apply the Pythagorean theorem: x = ML = sqrt(12^2 + 16^2) = sqrt(400) = 20.
